From 123af9043e93cb6f235207d260d50f832cdb5439 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2018 11:08:38 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] ASoC: au1x: Fix timeout tests in au1xac97c_ac97_read()

The loop timeout doesn't work because it's a post op and ends with "tmo"
set to -1.  I changed it from a post-op to a pre-op and I changed the
initial the starting value from 5 to 6 so we still iterate 5 times.  I
left the other as it was because it's a large number.

Fixes: b3c70c9ea62a ("ASoC: Alchemy AC97C/I2SC audio support")
Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Signed-off-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>

diff --git a/sound/soc/au1x/ac97c.c b/sound/soc/au1x/ac97c.c
index 29a97d52e8ad..66d6c52e7761 100644
--- a/sound/soc/au1x/ac97c.c
+++ b/sound/soc/au1x/ac97c.c
@@ -91,8 +91,8 @@ static unsigned short au1xac97c_ac97_read(struct snd_ac97 *ac97,
 	do {
 		mutex_lock(&ctx->lock);
 
-		tmo = 5;
-		while ((RD(ctx, AC97_STATUS) & STAT_CP) && tmo--)
+		tmo = 6;
+		while ((RD(ctx, AC97_STATUS) & STAT_CP) && --tmo)
 			udelay(21);	/* wait an ac97 frame time */
 		if (!tmo) {
 			pr_debug("ac97rd timeout #1\n");
@@ -105,7 +105,7 @@ static unsigned short au1xac97c_ac97_read(struct snd_ac97 *ac97,
 		 * poll, Forrest, poll...
 		 */
 		tmo = 0x10000;
-		while ((RD(ctx, AC97_STATUS) & STAT_CP) && tmo--)
+		while ((RD(ctx, AC97_STATUS) & STAT_CP) && --tmo)
 			asm volatile ("nop");
 		data = RD(ctx, AC97_CMDRESP);
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `sound/soc/au1x/ac97c.c`**
1. Changed the initial value of the timeout variable `tmo` from `5` to `6` in the first timeout loop.
2. Modified the timeout loop condition from `tmo--` to `--tmo` to ensure the decrement happens before the condition check in both timeout loops.

### Relationships Between Modifications
The modifications are related in that they both address the timeout mechanism within the `au1xac97c_ac97_read` function. The change from a post-decrement to a pre-decrement in the loop condition ensures that the timeout logic functions correctly, allowing for the intended number of iterations. The adjustment of the initial timeout value from `5` to `6` compensates for this change, ensuring that the loop still iterates the desired number of times (5 iterations) before timing out. Overall, these changes work together to fix the timeout behavior in the function.


The use of the post-decrement operation (`tmo--`) causes the timeout variable `tmo` to be decremented after the loop condition is evaluated. This means that when `tmo` reaches `0`, it is decremented to `-1` before the next iteration, potentially allowing the loop to run indefinitely if the condition remains true.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
tmo = 6;
while ((RD(ctx, AC97_STATUS) & STAT_CP) && --tmo)
```
Reason:

This allows the loop to iterate the correct number of times (5 iterations) and prevents it from running indefinitely by ensuring that `tmo` will eventually reach `0` and exit the loop correctly.
